sections: 2.3.1, 2.3.7 (toth row; new H+/OH- row), 2.4.7, 2.4.8, 2.4.11 (new D_H, D_OH rows), 2.4.13 (two new tests), 3.3, 3.5, 5.3 (TransportParams comment)
change: #23 TOTH transport. OLD: toth transported like any component, J_toth = -D̄_toth ∇TOTH with a 'buffer-capacity-weighted D' (2.3.7 toth row), TOTH including gelatin-bound protons. NEW: TOTH stays the per-cell conserved inventory (incl. T_gel n̄_gel), but its face flux is J_toth,ℓ+½ = Σ_{f mobile} -D̄_f,ℓ+½ (P_f,ℓ+1 - P_f,ℓ)/h - D̄_H Δ[H+]/h + D̄_OH Δ[OH-]/h, with P_f = T_f n̄_f(pH_ℓ), h = ½(Δ_ℓ+Δ_ℓ+1), and D̄_f,face the SAME harmonic-mean face D (r_f, s(t) in gel) used for that family's total. Gelatin has no flux; the top Dirichlet node uses bath speciation. New constants D_H = 8130, D_OH = 4600 um²/s at 20 °C (tracer 9.31e-5, 5.27e-5 cm²/s at 25 °C, recalled → assumed), r_gel 0.5, fields transport.proton_diffusion / transport.hydroxide_diffusion in kinetics.yaml (TransportParams). Jacobian (3.3): for TOTH transport keep only ∂J_toth/∂TOTH_ℓ = (Σ_f D̄_f β_f,ℓ + D̄_H β_H + D̄_OH β_OH)/(β_ℓ h), with β_f = -T_f dn̄_f/dpH, β_H = ln10[H+], β_OH = ln10[OH-], β_ℓ including gelatin. Drop the TOTH-vs-other-totals coupling (W-method), so overcoat/liquid blocks stay diagonal; the old buffer-weighted D exists only in J, never in f. Lateral (3.5): diffuse TOTH_mob = TOTH - T_gel n̄_gel(pH), with pH solved once at the start of L. Use a layer-constant D_toth,ℓ = (Σ_f D_f β̄_f + D_H β̄_H + D_OH β̄_OH)/β̄_mob,ℓ (β̄ = block-interior layer mean, β_mob excludes gelatin), then TOTH += TOTH_mob' - TOTH_mob. Same number of transforms. This is an assumed single-D approximation, checked by the new optional slow test test_lateral_toth_single_d (per-family reference on an edge strip, |ΔD| ≤ 2e-3). New tests: test_gel_equilibrium_no_toth_flux (unexposed, h_fog = 0, k_diss = k_pd = 0, s ≡ 1, gel pre-equilibrated with bath, 300 s: |pH - pH_bath| ≤ 1e-10, |J_toth| ≤ 1e-14) and test_immobile_buffer_retards_ph_front (one mobile buffer + gelatin, small perturbation: profile matches erfc with D/(1+β_gel/β_mob) within 1e-2 of amplitude). flux_mean and BulkTrajectory.toth signatures are unchanged; the TOTH column is now the mobile-species flux.

sections: 2.7.1, 2.7.2 step 4, 2.7.4, 10 (grain/statistical.py block), 9 #20
change: #24 statistical-mode variance. OLD: Var_count = T̄²(exp(Σ μ_c a_c²⟨x²⟩_c/A²) - 1) and Var(ε) = max(Var_bool - Var_count, 0)/T̄². NEW: Var_count = T̄²(exp(Σ_{c∈𝒞} μ_c q_c²) - 1), using the q_c = a_c(1+φ)x̄_c/A_pix that is actually sampled (x̄, not ⟨x²⟩). Var(ε) = max(Var_bool - Var_count, 0)/(T̄² + Var_count), because E[T_count²] = T̄² + Var_count, so the untruncated pixel variance equals Var_bool exactly. Var_bool formula unchanged; r̃_c = √(a_c(1+φ)⟨x²⟩^½/π); γ_mix includes all classes. boolean_excess_variance (grain/overlap.py) is unchanged; callers pass r̃ including (1+φ). New grain/statistical.py helpers: counted_classes(developed_areas_um2, pixel_um) -> bool (K,) and epsilon_variance(var_bool, mean_t, mu, q, counted). test_siedentopf_limit restated: Var_bool/(T̄² Σ μ a²⟨x²⟩/A²) → 1, checked at D = 0.001 with tolerance 0.1 %. The old 0.3 % at D = 0.01 fails because that ratio is κ(D), and kappa(0.01) = 1.0053. For x ≡ 1, Var_bool/Var_count → 1. New test test_statistical_variance_broad_x: one class, a/A_pix = 0.02, X = F/2, Y = F/3, D ∈ {0.3, 1}, 1e6 pixels; sample variance = Var_bool within 4 SE; truncation < 1e-4; Siedentopf limit of Var_bool equals the exact random-area value within 1e-4 relative.

sections: 2.7.1, 2.7.4, 6.6 step 2, 9 #20, 10 (grain/statistical.py)
change: #25/#48 validity condition. OLD: statistical mode valid only for p ≥ 4 r_max (r_max from the top class), else ValueError (test_validity_condition); §6.6 claimed p_g = 4 µm satisfies it. NEW: a class c with p ≥ 4 r_c (r_c = √(a_c/π), fully developed, fixed per frame) enters the Poisson count product (set 𝒞). Otherwise it is mean-only: deterministic factor exp(-μ_c q_c), no Poisson draw, and all its variance goes into ε through Var_bool - Var_count. T_pix = Π_{c∈𝒞}(1-q_c)^N_c · Π_{c∉𝒞} exp(-μ_c q_c) · (1+ε), truncated to [0,1]. There is no error any more. Var_bool stays the large-pixel (white-noise-equivalent) target, so aperture variance is p-independent and correct for aggregates ≫ disks. The aperture bias b_ap ≈ 1.15 r̃_eff/D_ap is recorded, with r̃_eff = √(Σ ν F (π r̃²)² / (π Σ ν F π r̃²)), and a warning fires if b_ap > 0.05. Readout.meta['grain'] gets mean_only_classes, b_ap, truncated_fraction. §6.6 keeps p_g = 4 µm (the claim is replaced) and warns when b_ap > 0.05 or truncated fraction > 1e-3. It adds a pre-fit Siedentopf check G_S = 1000·√(κ(1)·0.4343·⟨a²⟩/⟨a⟩/A_ap): T-Max starts more than 2× off 8 are dropped from multistart; Tri-X G_S is only recorded (17 is a check item, no leakage). The Tri-X prior centre gives G_S ≈ 80. Tests: test_validity_condition REMOVED; added test_mean_only_classes and test_trix_prior_centre_statistical (Tri-X prior centre at p = 6 and 4 µm runs without error and meta is populated; variance is not checked because truncation is large there).

#35 physical silver in grain. NEW: per pixel φ = r_CP·CP_ref·silver_physical / Σ_c CP_c silver_c (φ = 0 if the denominator is 0). Developed disks are enlarged uniformly: area a_c x̄ (1+φ) in q_c and r̃_c, and a_c x (1+φ) in micro mode. This keeps 0.4343 Σ μ_c q_c = D_Ag including physical silver. Base, halide and dye multiply the mean transmittance only. The uniform enlargement is assumed. test_statistical_mean_is_nutting now uses exp(-Σ ν F a x̄ (1+φ)) and includes a silver_physical > 0 case.

sections: 2.0.2 table, 2.5.3 paragraph, 5.8 film example, 7.1 (block F row, fixed-parameter sentence), 7.5 (table, new sensitivity paragraph), 7.9, 9 #32
change: #26 coated silver. OLD: m_Ag,coat assumed 4.0, said to be degenerate with CP_ref, and fixed. NEW: m_Ag,coat (grain.silver_coverage) is fitted per film in block F, lognormal prior centred on 4.0, bounds 2–6 g/m². §2.5.3 now explains why it is identifiable in principle: it sets C_c,z, Br/I/H+ released and developer consumed per unit density, exhaustion, adjacency amplitude, N_tot and L_e. If stage F fixes it at 4.0, sensitivity refits at {2, 6} g/m² per film go into the prediction band. §7.9 adds up to ≈2.5 days for up to 6 sensitivity refits. The block F count is now Tri-X 13–14 and T-Max 14–15; the §7.5 C rows are 13–14 and 14–15. In the 5.8 example, silver_coverage gains prior: lognormal and a PLACEHOLDER note.

sections: 2.0.2 table, 7.1 (block F, AR constraint bullet), 7.5, 9 #19 and new #31, 10 (calibrate/parameters.py comment)
change: #27 T-Max tablet thickness. OLD: t_g assumed 0.12, so AR ≥ 8 was just a box bound d_50 ≥ max(0.6, 8 t_g). NEW: t_g is fitted for T-Max, bounds 0.08–0.15, prior centre 0.12. T-Max is parametrised by (t_g linear, AR = d_50/t_g in log10 with bounds [log10 8, log10 19]) through a calibration-only parameter 'calibration:aspect_ratio', written back as grain.mean_diameter = AR·t_g. The d_50 ∈ [0.6, 1.5] µm bound becomes a one-sided penalty with scale 0.02 µm, in the same form as A_550. New §9 #31 covers the S/V growth scaling (2/t_g + 4/d: 29–17 µm⁻¹ against 6.7 for Tri-X). The report gives held-out sensitivity to t_g. If t_g is fixed, refits run at {0.08, 0.15}.

sections: 2.4.11 (C_sat,ref, ν_s, ν_b rows), 7.1 (C shared block 10 → 11), 7.5 (D 35 → 36, solvent text), 9 #9
change: #28 sulfite solvent exponents. OLD: ν_s literature(derived) 0.6 with bounds 0.3–2, fixed; ν_b literature(derived) 0.4 with bounds 0–1; anchor written '7.5e-5 N @ 0.010 N'. NEW: ν_s (solvent.sulfite_exponent) is fitted in the shared C block, linear with a uniform prior on 0.6–2 and kinetics.yaml initial value 1.0 (assumed). ν_b is assumed (extrapolated) 0.4 with bounds 0.3–1. The anchor reads Carroll & Hubbard 30 °C, 7.5e-5 M AgBr at 0.010 N = 0.005 M Na2SO3; extrapolated to 0.1 M this is 4.5e-4 (ν_s = 0.6) to 1.5e-3 M (ν_s = 1), as an order-of-magnitude reference only. The C_sat law and field names are unchanged. §9 #9 records the one-to-two-decade extrapolation.

sections: 2.3.7 (bromide, iodide rows), 3.6 halo formula and text, 3.8 test_halo_convergence row, 3.10 cost table, 4.5/4.6 worker memory and workers formula
change: #30 + #36 bromide D and halo. D_w: bromide 1420 → 1816 um²/s (tracer 2.080e-5 at 25 °C scaled by T/η). Iodide 0.94×D_Br → 1786 um²/s (tracer 2.045e-5), with gel ratio 0.5×0.94. OLD halo_um = min(3√(2·D_ref·t_q,max), 4.6 δ_max), D_ref = 1420. NEW halo_um = min(max_k 3√(2 D_k t_q,max/(1-ρ_k)), 4.6 δ_max) with ρ_k = exp(-t_a,min D_k (π/2δ_agit)²), where t_a,min is the shortest periodic agitation duration and ρ = 0 without periodic agitation. D_k is D_w(T) with T/η scaling only, no ionic factor. k also ranges over the lateral TOTH_mob D evaluated at the bath composition. Small tank at δ_agit 100 is 1047 µm (was 875); large tank and stand are 1380 µm. test_halo_convergence now runs small tank, large tank and stand at typical (50, 300 µm) and upper-prior (100, 500 µm) δ_agit, δ_max. Cost: halo 37 → 44 cells, overhead 1.66 → 1.81; chemistry 900 → 980 s, members 2500 → 2730 s, DCT 450 → 490 s, total 3900 → 4250 s. Worker memory 0.65 → 0.70 GB (344² cells, 1.89e6 members). The workers formula constant changes from 0.65 to 0.70 in floor((budget - 1.5)/0.70), so the default is 6 workers and about 12 min.

sections: 2.3.7 (sulfite, borate, bromide, iodide, silver r_gel; note †), 2.4.12 gel diffusion-time row, 5.8 sulfite example
change: #31 salt gel ratio. r_gel for salts (sulfite, borate, bromide, silver, H+/OH-) changes from 0.8 (literature) to 0.5 (assumed, bounds 0.3–0.8), extrapolated from Iwano KBr (0.8 at 8 %, 0.55 at 20 % gelatin) to the 30–45 wt % swollen emulsion. Iodide is 0.5×0.94. In the 5.8 example, sulfite gel_diffusion_ratio becomes {value: 0.5, source: assumed, bounds: [0.3, 0.8]}. The §2.4.12 Br⁻ gel diffusion times become 0.11/0.25/0.44 s.

sections: 2.4.12 (surface pH drop, closed-cell rows), 9 #2, 12.5
change: #29 buffer capacity. Recomputed with all families at pH 8.5: conditional total β = 33.3 mM/pH (sulfite 17.3, borate 8.4, HQ 6.9, metol 0.8) and ideal 92.0 (81.3, 5.9, 4.3, 0.5), plus gelatin about 2–4 mM/pH in gel cells. Surface pH drops change from 0.07/0.14/0.27/0.41 to 0.04/0.07/0.14/0.21 (conditional) and from 0.01/0.03/0.06/0.09 to 0.01/0.03/0.05/0.08 (ideal). The closed-cell β range is 0.03–0.09 M/pH. §9 #2 now reads total 92 → 33 (sulfite 81 → 17). No test values change.

sections: 2.4.5, 2.4.11 (new ΔH_Br row), 5.3 HalideParams comment
change: #33 temperature-dependent bromide adsorption. NEW: K_X(T) = K_X,20 exp(-(ΔH_Br/R)(1/T - 1/T_r)) for K_Br and K_I (same factor, assumed). The new field halides.adsorption_enthalpy is literature, fixed at -45 kJ/mol (Herz 1980), with -60 to -30 for sensitivity only. Kinetics.K_br and K_i are resolved at the solution temperature; no signature change.

sections: 2.4.13 test_arrhenius_scaling
change: #34. The condition now adds: speciation temperature-independent (all ionisation enthalpies and dpK/dT = 0, A(T) and pK_w fixed at 20 °C values), ΔH_Br = 0, no bromide. Assertion and tolerance (1e-3) unchanged.

#37 relabel only. The q₁ = 1/(1+ντ_i) closure is now described as a LAT §1.3(c) option-(ii)-type mean-field closure (assumed), not a minimal option (i). The text states that HIRF saturates at S_eff - 1 times m (1 stop for S_eff = 3) and that exposures shorter than about 1e-5 s show no further failure. Equations and tests unchanged.

sections: 6.9 step 3
change: #38. E_b = N_b · (h c/λ_b)[J] · 1e7 · 1e8 erg/cm², using D0 photon_energy_j, not the eV-valued E_ph,b of §2.1.2; symbols in §2.1.2 not renamed. New test test_spectral_energy_conversion (D1e): at 550 nm, 1 erg/cm² = 2769 photons/um² within 1e-3.

Before: the liquid grid was one geometric grid from 0 to δ_max (h₁ = δ_max(r−1)/(r^n−1)). During agitation, every liquid cell whose centre lay above δ_agit was clamped to the bath.

Now: the liquid has two sections.
- Lower: n_a = n_l//2 cells on [0, δ_agit]. Upper: n_l − n_a cells on [δ_agit, δ_max].
- Each section is geometric with ratio r_l. A section [a, b] with n cells has h₁ = (b−a)(r−1)/(r^n−1).
- Per profile: image 2+2, calibration 4+4, reference 8+8.

During agitation:
- The Dirichlet face is at h = δ_agit. The top lower cell's flux uses a half-cell distance: J = −D(C_bulk − C_ℓ)/(½Δ_ℓ).
- Upper cells are held at C_bulk(t), are not solved, and their inventory counts as tank.

At each agitation start, the upper section mixes into the tank:
- Its inventory excess ΔI_k = Σ_upper Δ_ℓ(C_k,ℓ − C_k,bulk) is added as a jump ΔC_bulk = +1e-15·(A_film/V_tank)·ΔĪ_k.
- In flux_mean and J̄_blk this jump appears as an impulse −ΔĪ_k/h for that step.
- The conservation tests count the held upper cells as tank.

Interface: column_grid(emulsion_dry_um, overcoat_dry_um, swelling_ratio, delta_agit_um, delta_max_um, profile). ColumnGrid gains delta_agit_um, n_a and agit_cell. develop/grid.py already matches.

New tests in §2.4.13:
- test_strip_smooth_in_transport: second-difference/ε² stable within 10 % at relative steps 1e-4/1e-5/1e-6 around δ_agit = 39/41/90 µm.
- test_dry_film_bromide_free_start.

Members (pixels) no longer take part in the time integration. Given cell-level κ_c,z(t), Λ_z(t) and C_Ag(t), the member equations are linear in p(n), so:
- X = Σ_n p(n) G_n, Y = Σ_n p(n) H_n, P_z = Σ_c Σ_n p(n) Q_c,z,n.
- dG_n/dt = κ(E_n − G_n), with E_n = 1 − e^{−h_n Λ_z}.
- dH_n/dt = 2κ(G_n − H_n).
- dQ_c,z,n/dt = k_pd n_c S_c G_n C_Ag/C_tot.

Each cell integrates 3·K·n_z·5 kernel states, driven by p̄_c,z(n), the area-weighted mean of its members' p computed once at the start. Schur elimination now applies to the kernels: a 3×3 lower-triangular block per (c, z, n).

Image path coupling:
- During development, members belong only to their own cell (nearest-cell coupling, replacing CIC in f).
- At the end and at each snapshot, a pixel's X, Y, P and F come from bilinear interpolation of the 4 neighbouring cells' kernels at the pixel centre, combined with the pixel's own p(n).
- Silver totals then differ from the cell chemistry by a second-order amount; this is stated in §3.8.
- Cells are independent, so a batch does both ROS2 stages at once, with no block-wide stage barrier.

Interface changes:
- Members becomes {exposure_volume, exposure_surface, layout: 'columns'|'raster', pixel_um, origin_um}; cell_index, cic_cells, cic_weights and area_weight are removed. Overlaps and bilinear weights are computed per row batch.
- run_ensemble outputs are per member: n_cells rows for columns, or inner pixels row-major for raster.

Tests:
- New: test_kernel_reduction_exact (≤ 1e-12; regrouping members ≤ 1e-13).
- test_member_schur_elimination_exact is kept.
- test_f_table_interpolation is removed.

sections: 2.4.2, 3.1, 3.3, 10 D1c FilmColumnModel
change: The 2-D F table is removed: before it was 201×121 bilinear on (log m, log Λ), error 3.4e-3, and only Lipschitz-continuous. Per emulsion cell and f-evaluation, 5 values E_n = 1 − exp(−h_n Λ_z) and ∂E_n/∂Λ = h_n exp(−h_n Λ_z) are computed and shared by all classes; F_c,z = Σ_n p_c,z(n) E_n. FilmColumnModel loses f_table, f_table_dlambda and log10_lambda. The §3.1 row 'latent / F table nodes' becomes 'latent table nodes 401/201/201 (cubic spline)', and a new row gives the liquid split.

Latent-table lookup changes from linear interpolation in log10 m to a not-a-knot cubic spline (C²), with coefficients precomputed in latent_table(). Negative values are clipped to 0, then the result is renormalised. Measured midpoint error at 201 nodes: linear 2.25e-3, spline 9.0e-6. test_latent_table_interpolation tightens from ≤ 1e-3 to ≤ 1e-4. Each member is looked up only twice per development: aggregation and synthesis.

sections: 3.4, 2.4.13 test_fixed_schedule_vs_reference, 12.6
change:
Before, the schedule restarted at h₀ at 0, at every agitation start and stop, and at every snapshot.

Now there are two kinds of time point:
- Reset points (restart at h₀): 0 and each agitation start only.
- Alignment points: agitation stops, snapshots and the end. A step that would cross one is cut to land on it, and the cut step does not advance j. A cut shorter than h₀/2 is folded into the previous step.

New step counts, image / calibration:
- Small tank, 7.5 min: 209 / 314 (old rule 293 / 454).
- Small tank, 12 min: 335 / 503.
- Large tank, 8 min: 160 / 248.
- Large tank, 12 min: 240 / 372.
- CI(t) run to 1.5 × 12 min with 15 s snapshots: small tank 407 / 623, large tank 312 / 492.

test_fixed_schedule_vs_reference now covers small and large tanks for both profiles: calibration ≤ 1e-3, image ≤ 2e-3. develop/schedule.py already implements this.

sections: 3.3, 2.4.6, 2.4.10, 10 D1c EnsembleResult
change:
Negative-concentration rule.

Before: reject any step leaving C < −1e-12 × the bath initial value and halve it, up to 4 times; record n_halvings.

Now:
- Fixed schedules never reject or split a step.
- All rate laws, and the speciation inputs, use the smooth positive part C⁺ = ½(C + √(C² + ε_c²)), ε_c = 1e-9 M (assumed). Transport and inventories use C itself.
- C_sat becomes C_sat,ref·([SO₃²⁻]⁺/0.1)^ν_s·(1 mM/√(([Br⁻]⁺)² + (1e-5)²))^ν_b; the previous max(Br, 1e-5) is gone.
- Each step records min C/s_k, with s_k = max(c_bulk(0), 1 mM). The minimum goes to meta['develop']['min_scaled_concentration'], with a warning below −1e-3.
- Adaptive (reference) mode treats min C/s_k < −1e-6 as a failed error test for the whole batch.

EnsembleResult.n_halvings is replaced by min_scaled_concentration: float. New test: test_dry_film_bromide_free_start.

sections: 3.7, 2.4.10 meta, 4.4, 10 D1c develop/prepass.py, 10 D1a state.py
change:
Before: the tank check passed if max|c' − c|/max(c(0), 1e-6 M) ≤ 1e-3. This could never pass for Br⁻, I⁻ and Ag, whose initial bath value is 0. The spec also asserted L ≤ 0.15 and a bound of 1.2e-3.

Now the check accepts on the output:
- Rerun the 65 prepass columns under the given trajectory c'_bulk (about 1 s).
- δ = max_b |M_b(c') − M_b(c)|/(M_b(c) + 0.3 g/m²), with M = Σ silver_c + silver_physical. Pass if δ ≤ 1e-3.
- On failure, rerun all blocks with c'_bulk and overwrite in place (FrameAssembler.reset()), at most 2 more passes.
- Diagnostics: L̂ = δ_{i+1}/δ_i; the depletion-normed change with s_k = max(|c_k(0)|, max_n|c_k(t_n) − c_k(0)|, 1e-6 M); the bulk pH change.
- L is no longer asserted; a warning is raised if L̂ > 0.5.

New interface: PrepassCheck{delta, depletion_change, ph_change, trajectory} and prepass_check(hist, film, solution, kin, schedule, tank, image_area_fraction, presoaked, current, block_flux, zero_flux).

meta['develop']['prepass'] keys become {bins, passes, delta (one per pass), contraction, depletion_change, ph_change}.

test_tank_prepass_check now asserts: depletion-normed trajectory difference ≤ 1e-2, bulk pH difference ≤ 1e-3, |ΔM| ≤ 3e-3 g/m².

Before, the chemistry cell was P·p with P = max(1, round(24/p)). Now it is fixed at Δx_c = 24 µm whatever the pixel pitch, with the grid anchored at the frame origin.

- Pixels are aggregated into cells by area overlap. When p > 24 µm one pixel spans several cells.
- The halo is H_c = ceil(halo_um/Δx_c).
- Pixel ownership: a block's inner cells [i₀, i₁) own the pixels whose centres lie inside, i.e. pixel rows ceil(i₀Δx_c/p − ½) … ceil(i₁Δx_c/p − ½) − 1. The block writes those pixels and calls mark() on them.
- A partial last cell (120: 2333.3 cells) counts its out-of-frame area as unexposed film in p̄.
- test_resolution_independence now covers p = 6, 9, 12 and 30 µm (box-mean density only at 30 µm).
- Cost no longer depends on resolution: about 1.5e6 cells per 135 frame.

sections: 3.10, 7.9, 10 D1d test_benchmark_image_path, 10 D1c done criterion
change:
Restated 24 MP budget: D-76 small tank 30 s/5 s, 7.5 min, 209 steps.
- Cells: 1.5e6 × 1.81 × 209 × about 12 µs per cell-step, about 6800 s. The 12 µs counts two stages of pH solve over 7 levels (2 × 2.66 µs), gel LU (2 × 0.51 µs), reactions, Jacobian, transport and the kernels.
- Members: about 60 s. DCT: about 570 s. Grain and readout: about 90 s (Var_bool alone 2.9 µs/pixel).
- Total about 7500 s on one core.
- 9 workers at an assumed effective ×6 gives about 21 min. A 12-min development takes about 33 min; large tank 8 min about 16 min. A preview costs about the same as a full frame.

test_benchmark_image_path:
- Before: a 2 MP crop extrapolated to ≤ 20 min.
- Now: time 1 block single-process and `workers` blocks in parallel, measure η, extrapolate t_b·ceil(24/workers) plus the other parts, and fail above 30 min. Log the cell-step cost and η.

D1c done criterion: the 35-step D-76 calibration strip (7.5 min, 314 steps) must run in ≤ 2 s single-core (was ≤ 1 s).

Calibration, rewritten as a table:
- About 3 ms per step for a 35–40-column call; about 1.4 s per condition; no cross-condition batching.
- Stage D objective about 23 s on 10 processes (assumed effective ×8). Jacobian about 7 min, rerunning only the conditions that read each parameter. One TRF iteration about 8 min.
- Multi-start 8×10 iterations plus the best 2 × 20 more: about 16 h. Stage C about 1.5 h per film. Stage E ≤ 10 h. Profile likelihood about 27 h.
- Total about 2–2.5 days (about 3 days if the effective parallelism is only ×6).
- differential_evolution is excluded from the budget.

New rows in the kernel-timing table: pH Newton, gel LU, parallel scaling, Var_bool.

sections: 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 10 D1a fieldstore.py / blocks.py / state.py / pipeline.py
change:
FieldStore:
- It is keyed by a store name, not a field key. Steps use name = f"s{step_index}:{key}"; a reused name raises ValueError.
- The backing file is '<name with / and : -> _>-<uuid4[:12]>.bin'.
- New: descriptor(name) -> FieldDescriptor(path, dtype, shape, offset), a picklable frozen dataclass, and open_field(desc, mode 'r'|'r+') -> np.memmap.

run_blocks:
- Same signature. With workers > 1, fn receives descriptors and writes its inner block into 'r+' outputs itself, and returns only small summaries in block order, never block arrays.

FrameAssembler:
- __init__ gains keyword name_prefix (store names are f"{name_prefix}{key}").
- New methods: descriptors(), mark(inner) and reset(). finish() checks each pixel was written or marked exactly once since the last reset.

RunContext gains store: FieldStore | None = field(default=None, compare=False, hash=False, repr=False). It is created and closed by the runner, kept out of the manifest and recipe_hash, and the store owns release().

Per-worker memory drops from 0.70 GB to about 0.5 GB, so workers = min(cpu, max(1, floor((budget − 1.5)/0.5))), which gives 9 by default.

New tests:
- test_fieldstore_unique_backing_files.
- test_run_blocks_workers_write_directly (each summary < 64 KB; bit-identical to workers = 1).
- test_assembler_each_pixel_once now covers mark and reset.

Fixtures and pseudo-components:

sections: 6.6, 6.7, 3.5, 7.2, 7.3 stage C, 7.4, 10 D1c Lateral, 10 D1e metrics
change:
Stage C objective components (MTF, granularity, inner searches).

MTF:
- Calibration uses a small-signal column pair per frequency: exposure e_z(1 ± ε M_X,z(ν)), ε = 1e-3, plus one uncoupled pair e_z(1 ± ε).
- The L step acts only on the difference mode: C_a,b ← C̄ ± ½(C_a − C_b)·exp(−D k² τ).
- MTF(ν) = 100·(D_a − D_b)(ν)/(D_a₀ − D_b₀), on the calibration profile with its fixed schedule, all frequencies in one call.
- Lateral.boundary gains 'pair', with wavenumber_per_um and columns ordered a0, b0, a1, b1, ….
- mtf_effective_exposure gains method: 'small_signal' (default) | 'periodic'. The m = 0.4 periodic strip is kept for validation only.

Granularity:
- The residual is the closed-form G_exp = 1000·0.4343·sqrt(Σ a_i² Var_pix)/(T̄ Σ a_i).
- GranularityResult gains expected_rms, and rms_granularity gains sample: bool.

Inner searches: fixed 4 secant iterations from a PCHIP initial guess, and brentq with xtol 1e-14. The old ±0.002 tolerance stop is removed.

Jacobian: computed by calibrate/objective.py; each column reruns only the conditions that read that parameter.

Multi-start: 8 starts × 10 iterations, then the best 2 continue for up to 20 more.

Profile likelihood is limited to ≤ 4 chemistry and ≤ 6 film parameters per film, at 8 grid points (was 10).

New tests: test_mtf_small_signal_limit (≤ 0.1 point), test_mtf_small_signal_vs_periodic (≤ 3 points at ≤ 30 c/mm), test_granularity_expected_vs_sampled, test_sparse_jacobian_matches_dense.

sections: 2.7.2, 10 D1c CellHistories / run_ensemble, 10 D1f micro/develop.py
change:
run_ensemble gains record_cells: int = 0. When it is > 0, EnsembleResult.cell_history is filled.

CellHistories moves from micro/develop.py to develop/ensemble.py:
- times_s (R,).
- lambda_clock (R, n_cells, n_z).
- kappa_integral (R, n_cells, n_z), K_z = ∫κ̃ dt. This replaces kappa_tilde (S+1, …).
- cell_spacing_um.

Values are recorded on the steps nearest 64 equally spaced times (the schedule is unchanged) and read back with monotone PCHIP interpolation. Grain development is x = 1 − exp(−(ℓS_c/V_c)(K(T) − K(t₀))). The cell history takes about 2 GB, against 10–32 GB with per-step storage.

develop_patch gains record = 64; a uniform exposure runs one column and broadcasts it.

New test: test_cell_history_thinning (≤ 1e-3).

New coding rule for per-block physics code:
- Not allowed: np.dot, np.inner, np.vdot, 1-D @, np.linalg.norm, einsum(optimize=True).
- Use instead: element-wise multiply plus np.sum, or einsum(optimize=False).
- Reason: on Accelerate, np.dot gave different bits for an 8-byte shifted copy of the same vector in 1267 of 2000 trials.

New test test_block_result_independent_of_alignment (D1c): one block recomputed from 8-byte-misaligned copies of its inputs must be bit-identical.

Test definitions:
- test_scatter_kernel_otf: compare against the box-filtered, aliased OTF Σ_{k=−8..8} P̂(ν + k/p)·sinc(νp + k), not P̂(ν).
- test_diffusion_into_slab: n_z = 8/16/32. Error ratio between refinements ≥ 3 at tD/L² ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 0.3}; error ≤ 2e-3 C₀ at n_z = 8 only for tD/L² ≥ 1.
- test_moving_reaction_front: dedicated 200-cell grid; front defined by integrated consumption x_f = consumed/C_s; 3 %.
- test_uniform_image_matches_strip: frame wider than two halos plus 2 blocks, infinite tank, same profile and schedule; pixels more than two halos from the edge must match ≤ 1e-10 (was ≤ 1e-12 everywhere).

sections: §6.3 step 2, test_iso_speed_on_kodak_tri_x, new test_dmin_star_same_operator; §6.5 D_min; §7.2 density row; §8.3 curve rows; §10 validate/metrics.py
change: Old: D_bf/D_min came from the zero-exposure patch on the simulated side and from the curve's left end (a proxy) on the Kodak side. New: every comparison with a Kodak characteristic curve uses D_min* = D_ref(x_left), where x_left = the reference's leftmost log H, and the simulated curve is evaluated at that same x_left; this gives log H_m*. CI compared with Kodak CI(t) curves or table cells uses the zero-exposure patch on the simulated side (Kodak assumed to plot from true base+fog, tagged assumed). New function d_min_star(log_h_ref, density_ref, log_h_sim, density_sim) -> (ref, sim). iso_speed signature now written as iso_speed(strip, *, density='type2', base_fog: float|np.ndarray|None=None); it already exists like this in code. §7.2 density window: [D_ref = D_min*+0.05, last point]; toe weight 0.5 for D < D_min*+0.1. §8.3: the 基雾 row becomes 左端密度 |D_sim(x_left) − D_ref(x_left)| (training ≤ 0.03, held-out ≤ 0.05). New one-sided row: D_sim(zero patch) ≤ D_ref(x_left) + 0.02. log H_m row → log H_m*. Toe densities are taken at the reference's log H_m* + 0.3 and + 0.6, both sides at the same log H. Curve RMS window starts at D_ref = D_min*+0.1. New test_dmin_star_same_operator: adding 0.02 D to the reference leaves the two-sided differences unchanged (≤1e-9).

change: Old: a 'time to CI' residual log10 t_sim − log10 t_ref with σ 0.012/0.02/0.04, XTOL and HC-110 σ doubled; thresholds 'equivalent time for ±0.03/±0.07 CI via local dCI/dt' plus an HC-110-only CI switch. New: every table cell, training and held-out, becomes an observation of kind 'table_ci' (x = t_cell, y = CI_aim, condition carries T, dilution and tank), residual CI_sim(t_cell) − CI_aim. CI_aim = 0.56 for F-4016/F-4017/J-24/J-86 tables (F-4016 prints none: assumed) and the column CI for J-109 Table 1. σ_cell = √(0.02² + (s_ref·0.072 min)²) × √n_class, where s_ref = slope of the same training pair's small-tank 20 °C reference CI(t) at CI_aim (computed once and fixed), and n_class = number of non-20 °C fitted cells in the (developer, dilution, tank, CI_aim) class. XTOL stock non-20 °C cells get a further ×2; the HC-110 doubling is removed. Thresholds: training RMS ≤ 0.03 and max ≤ 0.05 per pair; held-out ≤ 0.07 per cell. time_to_ci stays as a report-only function; new function ci_at_times(times_s, ci, at_s). change: Correlation handling (departs from the critic's '20 °C anchor + slope residual'; uses σ inflation instead). Characteristic-curve σ = 0.025·√(15/6) = 0.040.
